ledger.claim: The rider never left the pickup point. The GPS trace's rider track carries 85 qualifying fixes, all of them within 12.1 m of the pin (mean 8.1 m, minimum 4.3 m) and the rider's device records a single speed of 0.0 kph across the whole window, so the rider is far inside the 150 m rider-presence radius that fee_schedule sets for a LARGE_VENUE pickup. POL-NS-04 limb (c) is affirmatively satisfied on admissible fixes, not merely undecidable, and the rider's own track is a complete artifact at weight 1.0.

At 19:25:22, two and a half minutes after the driver tapped 'I'm Here', the rider sent 'im at the pickup, which car are you? i cant see you' - a request for the driver's position and a statement that the rider cannot see the vehicle, which is precisely the locating-or-coordinating content POL-NS-04 limb (a) names. A second message, 'hello? are you here', followed at 19:27:22. Both fall inside the waiting window that opened at the driver's 19:24:52 arrival and closed at the 19:32:46 cancellation.

The driver never answered. The chat log contains the rider's two messages and no driver message at all, both rider messages carry a null read timestamp, and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty. The driver therefore neither posted a reply within 120 seconds of the 19:25:22 message nor placed an in-app voice call at any point before terminating the trip: POL-NS-04 limb (b) holds, and the record shows no contact of any kind in the seven minutes and twenty-four seconds between the first message and the cancellation.

With limbs (a) to (c) of POL-NS-04 all satisfied the rider is exonerated and the cancellation fee is refunded in full. I do not contest that the driver's own track shows a 471-second in-geofence dwell and that limbs (a) to (d) of POL-NS-01 are otherwise met on the platform telemetry; but POL-NS-01 itself makes the fee chargeable only where no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces the conditions, and POL-NS-04 is exactly such a clause. The $4.50 cancellation_fee line, carried with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, must be returned to the rider.

No driver compensation is payable on this outcome. POL-NS-07 compensates the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, and POL-NS-04 grants the refund 'with no driver compensation payable'. The 0.8 compensation rate and the $3.60 driver_compensation figure shown in the ledger's derived block therefore have no application to this trip; the driver is left with no payout and the platform keeps nothing from a fee that was never chargeable.

The driver's counter-statement, 'I waited the full time', answers only the dwell question - which is not the defect the rider raises. A driver who holds position inside the geofence for the full wait but ignores two messages from a rider standing 12 m away has not performed the pickup; the chat log and the empty call record contradict any suggestion that he tried to make contact, and he has produced no reply, read receipt or call in evidence.

I disclose one impaired artifact as POL-GEN-02(1) requires: EV-ADVIS-02716-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and has no payload - no traffic advisory covers Tampines Mall in this window. Under POL-NS-06(i) a limb that would let separate in-geofence intervals be summed requires a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, and the clause says in terms that asserting a MISSING advisory triggers POL-NS-09 rather than exonerating anyone. The absent advisory therefore carries no fact for either side and leaves the POL-NS-04 outcome untouched.

No escalation trigger is in prospect, so this case should be decided now with the fee refunded rather than parked in human review. The trailing-90-day counterparty no-show counts are zero on both profiles; rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) names; and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check cannot trip on a driver with 2 no-show terminations in 30 days against 58 completed trips, because that clause requires 4 or more terminations AND a rate above 0.08. Both GPS tracks are complete artifacts at weight 1.0, so POL-NS-09(e) has nothing to bite on either.

POL-NS-01 limb (a) is made out on the platform's own record: the trip record logs a driver 'arrived' event for this trip, tapped by DRV-09716 at 19:24:52 and captured by PLATFORM_TELEMETRY, rather than being inferred from anything the rider says.

POL-NS-01 limb (b) is made out on the GPS and not merely on the driver's tap: the longest qualifying in-geofence run begins at 19:24:52 and dwell_start_offset_sec is 0.0, so the driver was inside the LARGE_VENUE arrival radius from the first in-geofence fix; the 'arrived' marker was therefore a true marker, not a false marker under POL-NS-05, and POL-NS-02's proximity test is satisfied by 47 qualifying in-radius fixes.

POL-NS-01 limb (c) is made out with room to spare: the driver held position inside the pickup geofence in one continuous run of 471 seconds across 47 consecutive in-geofence fixes, which is 2.6 times the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip and also above the 300-second minimum dwell the policy table sets for a LARGE_VENUE zone. POL-NS-06 returns no waiting-period shortfall at all (shortfall_sec -291), so the clause cuts for the driver and not against him.

POL-NS-01 limb (d) is made out: there is no boarding event anywhere on the record, and the driver terminated the trip at 19:32:46 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three reason codes the limb recognises, 292 seconds after the free waiting period expired. That is exactly the wait the driver's own statement describes when he says he waited the full time.

EV-ADVIS-02716-01 is MISSING — the admissibility pre-pass records issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT at weight 0.0, no advisory covering Tampines Mall in this window — so POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable and the driver does not need it: the dwell is a single continuous in-geofence run with no excursions, so no summing of separate intervals is required and the absence of an advisory is not evidence against this fee.

POL-NS-03 cannot decide this trip: it governs a driver stationary outside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin, and this trace places the driver inside the arrival radius throughout the hold, so no wrong-entrance analysis displaces POL-NS-01 limb (b) and the driver is not a driver who never reached the venue.

Compensation is payable under POL-NS-07 because the anti-farming check fails on both of its limbs: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4 the clause requires, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 58 is 0.034, below the 0.08 rate the clause also requires. Only those two fields are citable for this test; the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter is not the trailing-30-day figure and the driver does not rely on it.

ledger.claim: The driver's payment is 80 percent of the fee actually in force, so SGD 3.60 (0.80 x SGD 4.50), read from the net platform figure the ledger shows as charged — payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — and never from the rider's gross figure; the fare ledger's own derived money block confirms driver_compensation 3.60 and a scheduling fee of 4.50.

The case is decidable on the money and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is present: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that limb (d) requires, and the POL-NS-07 check does not trip, so the disputed SGD 4.50 should be ruled on rather than held for review.

The rider's device is on the trace — 85 of 85 rider fixes inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE presence radius, within 12 m of the pin — but that whole-track count does not by itself establish POL-NS-04 limb (c), which requires that presence for the majority of qualifying fixes across the waiting window, and the clause exonerates only a rider whose locating message went unanswered because the driver would not engage. The rider here named no entrance, block, tower or bay, sat beside a vehicle the driver had brought to the pin and held there for 471 seconds, and never boarded; the pickup failed at the point of boarding, not at the point of arrival, and the fee stands under POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-07.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties are looking at the same record, so here is what it shows.

The driver did arrive and wait. The trip record logs the 'I'm Here' tap at 19:24:52, the GPS trace shows an unbroken hold inside the pickup geofence of 471 seconds across 47 qualifying fixes (19:24:52 to 19:32:43), and the trip was cancelled at 19:32:46 under RIDER_NO_SHOW. Standing alone, the four limbs of POL-NS-01 are met, and the driver's statement that he waited the full time is true as far as the dwell goes.

But POL-NS-01 makes the fee chargeable only where no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, and POL-NS-04 displaces it here. All three of its limbs hold. (a) The chat log shows the rider sent two coordinating messages inside the waiting window — 'im at the pickup, which car are you? i cant see you' at 19:25:22 and 'hello? are you here' at 19:27:22. Each is a request for the driver's position and a statement that the rider cannot see the vehicle, which is exactly the content limb (a) names. (b) The driver neither replied nor called: the chat log contains no driver message and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty. (c) The rider's own track places the device within 12.1 m of the pin on all 85 qualifying fixes across the window, far inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius.

The driver's two arguments do not change this. The point that the rider 'named no entrance, block, tower or bay' fails because limb (a) is disjunctive — a request for the driver's position or a statement that the rider cannot see the vehicle each satisfies it, and both are present. The point that the rider 'never boarded' is true but irrelevant: the clause turns on the three limbs, not on boarding. Because POL-NS-04 displaces POL-NS-01, the $3.60 driver_compensation figure in the fare ledger does not arise — POL-NS-04 grants the refund 'with no driver compensation payable', and POL-NS-07 compensates only where no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces POL-NS-01.

On the evidence: EV-ADVIS-02716-01 (traffic advisory) is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. It carries no fact for either side; POL-NS-06(i) cannot be run without it, but nothing needs it, because the driver's hold is a single continuous in-geofence run. No artifact below weight 1.0 carries any deciding fact, so the confidence cap is 1.0.

No escalation applies. POL-NS-09(d) is not tripped — rider no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below 3, and the anti-farming check reads 2 no-show terminations against 58 completed trips, below both the count and the rate thresholds; the counterparty counts are 0; no two artifacts contradict each other; and no deciding fact rests on impaired evidence. Only the trailing-window counters are citable for those tests, and the driver's mention of prior_no_show_flags is a context-only lifetime counter that was expressly not relied on.

Amount: the full contested cancellation fee of $4.50 is refunded to the rider (fare_breakdown cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). That is below the $8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it executes on issue.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
